messages.author: 5ab11db47365dff1
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server query - serving content to the web
parts:
This may be obvious advice, but you need to make sure your virtual box is alive to the world.  For example, I use vagrant to run a virtual machine with parallels. When I boot vagrant, it sets up a locally accessible IP address and any requests to it get handled in the virtual server.

So, I don't just go to: localhost:3838.  I go to (ip address):3838.  You need to make sure that type of behavior is configured.

Consider setting up your virtual box using a service like vagrant.  It's quite nice for spinning virtual servers up and down.

https://www.vagrantup.com/

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Shiny server query - serving content to the web
parts:
Yeah, that's very different than "webpage not found". This is saying that the server could not be contacted (at least not on that port), so you have a networking or firewall problem.

1) Does your URL have port 3838? (It should)
2) Have you opened port 3838 with your cloud provider? In AWS this would be under Security Group.
3) Have you unblocked port 3838 on your Linux distro's built-in firewall? e.g. https://help.ubuntu.com/lts/serverguide/firewall.html

here is my config text

  GNU nano 2.2.6     File: /etc/shiny-server/shiny-server.conf                  

# Instruct Shiny Server to run applications as the user "shiny"
# run_as shiny;

# Define a server that listens on port 3838
server {
  listen 3838;

  # Define a location at the base URL
  location /users {
      #this is set up so that I can run apps sithout sudo
      run_as :HOME_USER:
      user_dirs;
  }
location /apps {
    run_as shiny;
    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server, /var/shiny-server/www/;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
      run_as :HOME_USER:
      user_dirs;
  }
location /apps {
    run_as shiny;
    # Host the directory of Shiny Apps stored in this directory
    site_dir /srv/shiny-server, /var/shiny-server/www/;

    # Log all Shiny output to files in this directory
    log_dir /var/log/shiny-server;

    # When a user visits the base URL rather than a particular application,
    # an index of the applications available in this directory will be shown.
    directory_index on;
  }
}
